newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state to sell off 40 pct of sixth miller.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state to sell off 40 pct of sixth miller.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills said on Wednesday it was offering investors at least 2.4 million shares in East Delta Flour Mills, or 40 percent of the equity, at a fixed price of 31 pounds a share.
The two-day flotation, part of the government's privatisation programme, will start on September 22 with Banque Misr acting as agent, the parent company said.
Individual investors are offered 1.2 million shares, it added. This amount can be increased if demand justifies.
The company is offering mutual funds and financial institutions 600,000 shares. The miller's employees are allocated the traditional portion of 10 percent.
Shareholders will be eligible for a dividend of at least 3.00 pounds for the financial year which ended on June 30, 1996, the company said.

The state regards milling firms as strategic and once said it would not sell more than 40 percent of its stake but heavy demand for an earlier privatisation, Central and West Delta Flour Mills, persuaded it to change its mind in that case.
East Delta Flour Mills manufactures bread and pasta for distribution in nine eastern provinces.
The firm increased net profits for the 1995/96 financial year to 27.78 million pounds from 27.66 million a year earlier.
